paper_title: Memorization and Knowledge Injection in Gated LLMs
caption: Analysis on the embedding quality in Llama intermediate layers. Correct gate rate is computed as the rate of question embeddings which have the maximum inner product with the relevant passage embedding. It is computed for each dataset partition, which has 50 passage samples. Shaded area is the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions. We found that embeddings at the input of MLP layers are better than at the input of attention layers. We choose to use last MLP layer input as embedding in the main experiments of MEGa.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average correct gate rate across embedding layers for two different datasets (Character and Wiki) and two different network components (Attention input and MLP input), with the x-axis representing the embedding layer number ranging from 0 to 30 on a linear scale, and the y-axis representing the average correct gate rate ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale. The shaded regions around each line indicate the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions, with each partition containing 50 passage samples. The blue solid line (Character Attention input) starts at approximately 0.1 at layer 0, rises to about 0.8 at layer 5, then declines sharply to around 0.3 at layer 10, recovers slightly to about 0.5 at layer 15, and then fluctuates between 0.5 and 0.7 until layer 30. The blue dashed line (Character MLP input) begins near 0.8 at layer 0, remains relatively stable around 0.8 to 0.9 until layer 10, dips to approximately 0.6 at layer 12, recovers to around 0.8 by layer 15, and then stays above 0.8 until layer 30. The red solid line (Wiki Attention input) starts at approximately 0.2 at layer 0, increases to about 0.8 at layer 5, drops to around 0.4 at layer 10, rises again to about 0.6 at layer 15, and then oscillates between 0.5 and 0.7 until layer 30. The red dashed line (Wiki MLP input) begins near 0.8 at layer 0, remains above 0.8 until layer 10, dips to approximately 0.6 at layer 12, recovers to around 0.8 by layer 15, and then stays above 0.8 until layer 30. Across all layers, the MLP input lines (dashed) consistently exhibit higher correct gate rates than their corresponding Attention input lines (solid), indicating better embedding quality at the MLP layer inputs.
